claim: Recommendations are chosen per viewer at load time from history + context
official_youtube_support: YouTube Help: recommendations personalized by watch history/context (2 official pages per repo validation 2026-09-04)
internal_senior_health_evidence: Bathing (507K) and eyesight (569K) winners had ~0 web-search demand (GT-20, GT-21) - consistent with non-search (browse/suggested) discovery
external_evidence: Ares/Elias hits spawn 8-9 copies within days that mostly get 1-150 views (C12, C13)
counterexample: Traffic-source data UNKNOWN; cannot prove browse share
practical_implication: Design for recommendation surfaces (thumbnail/title click appeal to a defined senior viewer), not keyword search alone

claim: Subscriber response is learned separately from non-subscribers/new viewers
official_youtube_support: Official: personalization per viewer; segment mechanism not confirmed
internal_senior_health_evidence: Okoro breakout on a 3,800-sub channel (494K) and Aliza persona channel 22.9K subs with a 941K video: reach not bounded by subscribers
external_evidence: Fit Lit Health 65.9K subs, 11 uploads >250K in 5 weeks
practical_implication: New channel can reach non-subscribers from video 1; do not wait for a subscriber base

claim: Evergreen videos can get most views long after publication
official_youtube_support: Official: videos evaluated while publicly available
internal_senior_health_evidence: Live counts rose after acquisition: Ares pee 350,960 -> 404K; Elias pee 18,355 -> 51K; Ares sleep 1.475M -> 1.6M (C05, C06)
external_evidence: Gentle Health bath video 602K from ~1 year ago still ranks first (C10)
counterexample: Most cohort videos are <6 months old - long-tail unobservable
practical_implication: Prefer evergreen senior problems (falls, nocturia, bathing) over news pegs for the core library

claim: No single metric; long-term viewer value
internal_senior_health_evidence: Title/thumbnail feature effects are weak and inconsistent (e.g., doctor persona 1.08x vs 1.07x)
counterexample: Satisfaction/retention data UNKNOWN for all cohort videos
practical_implication: Do not optimize a single packaging trick; the evidence says no single feature dominates

claim: Align channel with audience; recommendations still distinguish format preferences
official_youtube_support: Todd Beaupre (on record): 'Same audience? Same channel'
internal_senior_health_evidence: SHH mixes long-form and one Short (5 dangerous fish Short 2,441 = 0.26x)
external_evidence: Colon/constipation demand served mostly by clinician Shorts (C09)
counterexample: Single Short in cohort - weak test
practical_implication: Keep one senior-health channel; treat Shorts as a separate experiment track

claim: Suggested videos can cross topics via broader interests / co-viewing
official_youtube_support: Official: co-viewing signal exists; cross-topic scope unconfirmed
internal_senior_health_evidence: Okoro kidney video (11.3K) ends pointing to the foot breakout; neuropathy (100.9K) followed foot breakout by 18 days - adjacent-topic spillover plausible
external_evidence: Pair 7 loser (kidney + diabetes, 45 views) also adjacent to breakout topic but posted 2 months later
practical_implication: Build adjacent follow-ups inside ~3 weeks of any hit and link them explicitly

claim: New channels can be matched to viewers without history
official_youtube_support: Official: 'give as many videos as possible a chance'; Hype feature for small channels
internal_senior_health_evidence: Okoro: 25 uploads at ~114-801 views then a 494K video on a 2-month-old channel; Aliza cohort channel 217 median then 219K copy
external_evidence: Fit Lit Health relaunch breakout (C-CH); Dr. Aliza Wright Senior Health 941K on a new channel
counterexample: Most copy channels stay at 1-150 views (C03, C12, C13)
practical_implication: A new channel can break out early - but only with packaging/topic that wins on its own merits

claim: Subscription does not imply interest in every upload
internal_senior_health_evidence: Post-hit baselines did not lift: SHH median before/after 3.09M video 9,539 vs 9,418; Okoro recent-10 median 75
external_evidence: TopHealthTips 336K subs, recent uploads 2.3K-28K after a 1-2M cluster
practical_implication: Expect each upload to earn its own audience; a hit does not raise the floor

claim: Near-identical templated repetition can be treated as spam/inauthentic
official_youtube_support: YouTube monetization policy on inauthentic/mass-produced content
internal_senior_health_evidence: Ares/Elias share thumbnail text incl. identical typos; inside the twin, re-runs >=15 days later lost 4 of 6, while network-wide late copies by stronger channels usually won (14/16 at >=29 days)
external_evidence: >=6 verbatim copies of Okoro's foot title at 2-53 views; >=9 anesthesia copies at 1-2.3K
counterexample: Early copies can win (Fit Lit 412K and Dr Stick 190K copying Elias eyesight within 1-3 weeks)
practical_implication: Never re-run a title that already exists; build original angles (policy + performance risk)

claim: Watch history is an important input
internal_senior_health_evidence: Clove franchise: SHH ran 41 clove videos (34% of uploads, 73.1% of views); 4 of top-5 channel videos are clove - viewers of one clove video plausibly see the next
external_evidence: Knowhow creatinine series collapses after 1 hit (121K -> 1.2K/969/374)
counterexample: 27 of 41 clove entries stayed below 3x; exact repeats of the 3.09M format drew 8.7K-12.9K
practical_implication: Series work when each episode is genuinely different; repetition alone does not carry

claim: Semantic IDs from content understanding help cold-start matching
official_youtube_support: Published YouTube research on semantic IDs
internal_senior_health_evidence: Same-topic videos across channels are served to similar audiences (sister-channel inversion pattern)
external_evidence: Persona clone channels ('Dr. Ares Smith Senior Health!', 'Wellness After 70 - Dr. Elias') get ~1-122 views
practical_implication: Topic clarity per video matters; persona copying does not transfer reach

claim: Larger/fewer homepage thumbnails improved long-form viewing
internal_senior_health_evidence: Winning thumbnails are legible single-idea designs (Thomas, Ares, Okoro breakout)
practical_implication: Design thumbnails that read at large homepage size and small mobile size

claim: Shorts and long-form should never share a channel
internal_senior_health_evidence: Only one cohort Short; not testable
practical_implication: Do not adopt the absolute rule

claim: Specific content for a clearly understood viewer beats subscriber totals
counterexample: Subscriber data only for 4 of 6 channels
practical_implication: Define the viewer (60-85, managing 1+ chronic condition/medication) and write every title for them

claim: Find differentiated value; do not be the Nth interchangeable treatment
internal_senior_health_evidence: Nth-copy failures across the network (C03, C05, C12, C13)
practical_implication: Differentiate by evidence quality and original demonstration - the one thing mills cannot copy

claim: Launch with several linked videos (coherent journey)
official_youtube_support: Official: session/linked viewing documented; launch-cluster effect unproven
internal_senior_health_evidence: Doctor Thomas's 3 hits were 3 fall/walking videos within 10 days (Jun 11-21)
external_evidence: SHH's random early topics (nuts, fish) failed
practical_implication: Launch the mobility pillar as a linked 3-video mini-series

claim: Develop repeatable formats into recognizable shows
internal_senior_health_evidence: SHH clove franchise; TopHealthTips 'exercise for symptom' cluster
practical_implication: One format per pillar, episodes must differ materially

claim: Structure scripts with early direct answers for AI-answer citation
internal_senior_health_evidence: Winners withhold the answer early (thumbnail answer withheld 1.90x)
practical_implication: Do not adopt; conflicts with observed curiosity mechanics

claim: Seek questions not already covered well; add net-new information
internal_senior_health_evidence: Whitespace: Mounjaro/Wegovy pill, creatine, mini-stroke in women, BP timing trial - no cohort coverage (GT-25, GT-32, GT-11, GT-13)
counterexample: Demand for whitespace topics is unproven on YouTube
practical_implication: Use whitespace as 20-30% experiments, not the launch core
